docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Civil motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Civil motions and page limits (trap): Memoranda supporting or opposing a motion are capped at 20 pages and replies at 10. Extensions are rare and must be requested in writing at least 14 days before the motion is filed. No supplemental briefs after the reply without leave. Times New Roman no smaller than 12 point (Courier no smaller than 10); footnotes no more than one size smaller, used sparingly. Paginate multi-page exhibits internally from 1 and cite as “Ex. A at 7.” Searchable (OCR or hyperlinked) filings are encouraged. Cite cases to the specific page, preferring Westlaw over Lexis for unpublished cases; list the more authoritative source first; and cite statutes to the specific section and subsection (no “et seq.”).

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Meet and confer and waiver (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Meet and confer and waiver (trap): In counseled cases, meet and confer thoroughly before filing any motion, including summary judgment. Plaintiff’s counsel should weigh the claimed pleading defects and often agree to an amendment that would cure a curable defect. All purely legal issues must be raised by timely pretrial motion; failing to raise a dispositive legal issue before the dispositive-motion cut-off may waive it.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Courtesy copies, proposed orders, and contact
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Courtesy copies, proposed orders, and contact: No paper courtesy copies of pleadings or exhibits unless ordered. Email every proposed order in Word to tlnorders@caed.uscourts.gov in addition to e-filing the PDF, with the case number and “proposed order” in the subject line (L.R. 137(b)). Do not contact the judge or chambers staff by phone, email, or other ex parte means; appropriate inquiries go to the courtroom deputy. Promptly notify the court whenever a case may be transferred by the JPML, whether or not you are a party to the JPML filing.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Ex parte, TROs, and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Ex parte, TROs, and extensions (trap): Use L.R. 233 for administrative relief; an ex parte application is for relief unavailable that way and is usually decided on the papers. Contact the opposing party first, state whether an opposition will be filed, and attach an affidavit on the need, the inability to get a stipulation, and why the matter can’t be noticed under L.R. 230. Oppositions are due within 48 hours (72 hours if the application is filed on a Friday). For TROs and injunctions, the court typically won’t rule until at least 24 hours after the opposing party is served. Stipulations extending schedule dates are not effective until approved; agreement alone is not good cause, and witness or counsel unavailability rarely is. File well in advance, listing the existing and other scheduled dates and any prior extension requests and their outcome.

docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Discovery and experts: Discovery disputes go to the assigned magistrate judge, with “DISCOVERY MATTER” in the caption and no courtesy copies to Judge Nunley. Designate experts with signed Rule 26(a)(2)(B) reports per the Initial Pretrial Scheduling Order, identifying each as percipient, retained, or both. A late designator’s supplemental list is limited to rebuttal, and undesignated experts testify only on the good-cause showing the order describes. Finish expert discovery in time for the dispositive-motion deadline.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Sealing: Nothing is sealed without prior approval, under L.R. 141 and 140. In criminal cases, email the request to seal, a Word proposed order, and the documents to tlnorders@caed.uscourts.gov after e-filing the notice.

A settlement conference may be set at the final pretrial conference or earlier on joint written request, before a randomly assigned magistrate judge or through VDRP. An early settlement conference needs a stipulation and proposed

docs.x: Judge William B. Shubb, E.D. Cal.. Trial: Trial hours are usually Tuesday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., confirmed at the pretrial conference, trial confirmation hearing, or first day of trial. docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Motions (trap): The clerk schedules motions when received, so leave the hearing date and time blank. The court requires strict compliance with LR 7.1(a) on seeking concurrence, generally enforces LR 7.1(d) on responses, and is not liberal in extending page limits absent special circumstances. The court generally prepares its own orders. Dispositive motions are generally not referred to a magistrate judge; referred motions are usually discovery motions.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Conferences and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Conferences and scheduling: A scheduling conference is routinely set after the Answer is filed, where motion cutoff, discovery cutoff, final pretrial, and trial dates are set. Request an additional status conference by motion if the other parties do not agree, or by telephone call if all agree. Status and pretrial conferences may be held by telephone unless the matter is complicated or should settle before discovery.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: Discovery time depends on complexity and need, and once set the dates are adhered to. Witnesses must be disclosed before the discovery cutoff. Parties must meet to narrow disagreements before any discovery motion; discovery motions are generally referred to a magistrate judge. Deposition disputes should be handled by counsel, but if needed the parties may call the court and put the dispute on the record if the judge is available. The discovery cutoff may be extended by stipulation if no other date in the pretrial order is affected.

docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. TROs, removal, and class actions: TRO and preliminary-injunction briefing normally follows LR 7.1 timing. For an ex parte TRO or preliminary-injunction motion, the other side must be notified and its phone number given to the court. No class-certification requirements beyond the Federal Rules (the page cites “Fed.R.Civ.P. 3”).

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Mediation and settlement
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Mediation and settlement: All civil diversity cases are routinely referred to mediation under LR 16.3; on request of counsel, another ADR method may be used instead. The judge routinely becomes involved in settling jury cases and may refer a non-jury case to another judge for a settlement conference. A settlement conference can be scheduled before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial and trial date (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial and trial date (trap): The joint final pretrial order (LR 16.2) is due 5 days before the final pretrial conference, which is typically held 1 week before trial. Trial adjournments are not often granted; give as much notice as possible of a conflicting trial.

docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Trial preparation (trap): Exchange exhibits at least 1 week before trial, numbered consecutively; a bench book is encouraged. Parties keep custody of their exhibits during trial and after trial pending appeal. Trial briefs must be exchanged before trial. Motions in limine are due no later than 1 week before trial and are generally heard the morning of trial. Joint jury instructions are filed at the beginning of trial. Bench trials: file proposed findings and conclusions before trial ends; findings are generally made orally.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Jury selection and courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Jury selection and courtroom conduct: Striking method; the court conducts preliminary voir dire and allows reasonable voir dire by counsel, and challenges are handled so jurors do not know who excused them. In criminal cases two alternates are normally used and are not told they are alternates until the end. Only one lawyer per party may examine a given witness. Ask permission to approach the witness or bench; stand to speak, but you need not stay at the podium and may approach the jury box. Time limits on openings and closings are possible. The jury is charged before closing arguments and is given a copy of the instructions. Jurors typically may not take notes unless both sides agree.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: The court handles most pretrial matters, follows the court-rule cutoff dates, and enforces the standing orders’ discovery and motion cutoffs. Trial briefs are not always required; witness lists are preferred. The government is urged to disclose Jencks material before trial. Jury questionnaires are allowed in extraordinary cases, and instruction disputes are resolved at a hearing on the record.

docs.t: Judge Bernard A. Friedman (E.D. Mich.) — Pleas and sentencing
docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Pleas and sentencing: The court accepts Alford and nolo contendere pleas, sometimes over government objection, and will accept a plea agreement capping the sentence at a stated period above the bottom of the guideline range. A presentence report is required even with no custody and for corporate defendants, unless both sides waive it; if waived but the defendant asks for one, it will be ordered. Guideline disputes are typically resolved at sentencing, and a rejected Rule 11 agreement is announced in open court. Self-reporting may be allowed.

Label all exhibits and highlight the relevant portions. Include copies of the main cases and other authority relied on, with the relevant parts highlighted. Transcript or deposition exhibits must include the entire transcript, relevant portions highlighted, printed four pages per page and double-sided.

If the parties resolve a pending motion, email the Case Manager by the

Challenges to experts under FRE 702, 703, or 705 are due by the summary judgment deadline.

docs.x: Judge Brandy R. McMillion, E.D. Mich.. Expert disclosures are due no later than 90 days before trial and Rule 26(a)(3) pretrial disclosures no later than 30 days before trial, unless the order sets other dates.

docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Motions and concurrence (trap): L.R. 5.1, L.R. 7.1, and the Electronic Filing Policies and Procedures are strictly enforced for all motions. docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: The court usually allows 4–6 months for discovery. docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. TROs and injunctions: The court follows Fed. R. Civ. P. 65 and grants ex parte relief only in extraordinary circumstances. Briefing is typically accelerated, and hearings are set as the urgency requires.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Removal
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Removal: If jurisdiction is questionable, the court issues an order to show cause or waits for a motion to remand. It will not dismiss or remand sua sponte without notice to the parties.

docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing and hearings
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Briefing and hearings: No briefing schedule is usually issued; LR 7.1(e) and Rule 6 deadlines apply and are enforced even if the hearing is far off. Bring a proposed order to the hearing. If a pending motion is resolved, email the case manager within 1 business day and the movant must file a notice withdrawing it. If a case settles, notify chambers by email by the next business day.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave. Concurrence certification (trap): The first paragraph of every motion must certify L.R. 7.1(a) compliance with one of four statements (or one substantially similar): counsel spoke or met with opposing counsel, who expressly denied concurrence; counsel wrote to opposing counsel, who expressly denied concurrence; counsel wrote and 3 business days passed without express agreement; or counsel made no or a limited attempt because of exceptional circumstances stated with specificity. Modify the statement where a party is unrepresented. A motion without the certification will be struck.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Briefing (trap): The L.R. 7.1(d)(3) page limit is enforced; oversized briefs require a motion giving specific reasons. No briefing schedule issues: L.R. 7.1(e) and Rule 6 dates are enforced even when the hearing is far off, and untimely filings risk striking, loss of oral argument, and fees. Extensions are by motion. Only one response and one reply. Sur-replies, supplemental briefs, notices, or other papers in response to a motion without leave will be stricken, and a response may not be combined with a counter-motion. All supporting materials go in an appendix with a table of contents, tabbed exhibits, and relevant portions highlighted, plus the full text of unpublished authority not on Westlaw. Cite with page references, and for transcripts provide the cited pages with enough context. Cite unpublished cases to Westlaw, not Lexis. No courtesy copies

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave, and challenges to several counts go in a single motion. The brief must open with a “Statement of Material Facts” in numbered paragraphs, each with specific record citations. The response opens with a “Counter-statement of Material Facts” using the same numbering, admitting or contesting each fact with record citations, and may add a “Statement of Additional Material Facts.” If it does, the reply opens with a “Reply to Counter-statement of Material Facts.” All of these fact statements count toward the page limit; no other fact recitation is required.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery and deadlines
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Discovery and deadlines: Unless page 1 of the order says otherwise, parties may not be added or pleadings amended more than 14 days after the scheduling order, absent good cause. Witness lists (separating will-call from may-call) and exhibit lists are filed, and exhibits are exchanged by the exhibit-list date. “Expert” includes non-retained experts such as treating physicians; generic witness categories are not allowed. Experts must be available for deposition within 14 days after their disclosures. Serve discovery early enough for responses before the cutoff; no discovery after the cutoff absent good cause. Move to compel promptly once grounds appear and efforts to resolve are exhausted.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Adjournments, stipulated orders, and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Adjournments, stipulated orders, and contact (trap): Events before the dispositive and expert motion deadline may be adjourned by proposed stipulated order, so long as no later date moves. Anything on or after that deadline requires a prompt written motion showing good cause, except that a request may be emailed to the case manager (copying opposing counsel) within 1 week after the order issues. Proposed and stipulated orders are not e-filed; submit them through CM/ECF Utilities in Word or WordPerfect. Counsel may contact the case manager only on administrative or scheduling matters, and may not contact law clerks unless expressly authorized.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Sealing and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Sealing and protective orders: Proposed protective orders must include the judge’s required sealing language (no advance authorization; a motion or stipulated order under L.R. 5.3 stating authority, items, reasons, inadequacy of alternatives, and legal authority). With a motion to seal, submit a proposed order stating the particular reason through Utilities to the district judge or the referred magistrate judge. If granted, e-file the documents with a sealed designation.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Motions in limine and trial objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Motions in limine and trial objections (trap): Each party may file only one motion in limine (up to 25 pages) absent leave, by the “all other motions” deadline. Objections to testimony or exhibits must be raised by timely motion unless good cause excuses delay. Exchange all proposed exhibits at least 14 days before the “all other motions” deadline. Unresolved objections go in a separate motion (motion and response up to 15 pages each, attaching the exhibits) filed by that deadline, or they are waived. De bene esse depositions must be finished at least 21 days before that deadline, with page-and-line designations served at least 14 days before it. Unresolved objections go in a separate motion (up to 15 pages) by the deadline, or they are waived.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Settlement and ADR
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Settlement and ADR: The court conducts settlement conferences in jury cases and refers non-jury cases to another judicial officer. Trial counsel, natural-person parties, representatives with full and final authority for other parties and controlling insurers, and an authorized representative of any governmental party must attend in person; phone availability or counsel’s claimed authority does not satisfy this. Facilitation with a facilitator of the parties’ choosing is encouraged; the court picks one if the parties cannot agree. Case evaluation under L.R. 16.3 is by the court’s form order submitted through Utilities and must finish, including the accept/reject period, at least 7 days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Joint final pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Joint final pretrial order (trap): The judge’s requirements replace L.R. 16.2(b). Counsel must confer face to face (plaintiff initiates), and plaintiff submits the proposed JFPO in hard copy and through Utilities on the set date. It may not add claims or defenses. For each claim and defense, state the elements, principal supporting facts (contested or not), authority for every element, and each party’s damages calculation. List witnesses with the specific subject matter of their testimony and expert opinions with particularity, list exhibits by offering party with any pending objection motion, and identify other evidentiary issues with good cause for not raising them by motion in limine. Submit at the same time a settlement letter, docketed joint agreed jury instructions, a joint disputed-instructions document (each side’s position up to 2 pages per i

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Trial dates are set in every civil case and not adjourned absent good cause. Trials generally run 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., with occasional afternoon sessions. The court conducts voir dire and allows follow-up questions by counsel. Jurors may take notes and ask witnesses questions, and the court sets time limits on openings and closings after consulting counsel. Each party submits a binder of its proposed exhibits, with exhibit lists that include “Admitted?” and “Notes” columns, at least 2 business days before trial. Counsel keep custody of admitted exhibits, provide a copy for every juror when publishing, and give the court a complete admitted set before deliberations. Trial briefs are optional (at least 7 days before trial). Disclose electronic display aids by the final pretrial conference and supply the equipment. The court gives customary ope

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Patent cases and removal
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Patent cases and removal: Patent cases follow the judge’s Model Rule 26(f) Report and timeline, with trial about 24–26 months after the scheduling conference and liability and damages normally bifurcated before the same jury. A default protective order is entered automatically, and an off-the-record technology tutorial precedes claim construction briefing. Opening and response claim construction briefs are limited to 30 pages and the reply to 7. Live testimony at the Markman hearing requires a written motion and is typically limited to one hour per side. After removal, each party must re-file its state-court answers, pleadings, pending motions, and related responses and replies as separate docket entries; unre-filed state motions are generally not considered.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Page: courtesy copies of all dispositive motions, responses, and replies, mailed no later than 1 business day after e-filing. Use the e-filed version with the file stamp on each page, firmly bound on the left (call chambers if stapling or spiral binding is not possible). Include copies of the main supporting cases (Westlaw printouts strongly preferred; no boilerplate authority) and all exhibits, printed double sided with the relevant parts highlighted and file stamps on the exhibits. The older sample civil and criminal orders require courtesy copies of all motions and briefs, sent the same day by first-class mail or hand-delivered by the next business day; the civil sample bars rubber bands and binder clips, and the criminal one bars prong fasteners.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Briefing (trap): Per the sample case management order, every brief must contain a table of contents, a table of authorities, and an index. Cite docket and page for any opposing argument referenced, and focus on a few recent controlling cases rather than boilerplate or string cites. LR 7.1(e) deadlines apply unless the hearing notice says otherwise; sur-replies are generally not permitted. Extensions of time or extra pages require a concise stipulation and order filed at least 1 week before the brief is due. If the parties resolve a pending motion, or the case settles, notify chambers in writing by the next business day by email to the case manager or by fax.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Chambers contact and orders
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Chambers contact and orders: No ex parte communications. Contact the case manager or judicial assistant only on procedural, administrative, or scheduling matters; contacting law clerks is not permitted unless authorized. Proposed and stipulated orders are not e-filed; submit them in Word through CM/ECF Utilities. No pro hac vice admission; non-Michigan bar members must have local counsel.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling conference and discovery
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling conference and discovery: File a Joint Case Management Report/Discovery Plan at least 5 business days before the conference, addressing under separate headings: related cases, jurisdiction, factual summary, legal issues, amendments, discovery (including any Rule 502(d) order), ESI (including the district’s Model ESI Order), settlement, magistrate-judge consent, trial, and miscellaneous. Discovery starts after the meet-and-confer. Appear in person; a telephone conference may be allowed for good cause through the case manager. Typical deadlines: amendments 30 days after the conference; proponent experts 30 days after fact discovery; rebuttal experts 30 days later; expert cutoff 30 to 45 days after that; dispositive motions and expert challenges (FRE 702, 703, 705) 30 to 45 days after expert discovery. docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial and trial (trap): Sample order: Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures 60 days and motions in limine 30 days before the final pretrial conference (responses in 10 days, replies in 5); the final pretrial order through Utilities 2 weeks before. Trial counsel with settlement authority must attend the conference. One week before the conference, submit a Joint Bench Book (administrative section with trial length in half-day blocks, joint theory of the case read to the jury, voir dire requests of no more than 15 questions, witness list with exam times, agreed and disputed jury instructions and verdict form, evidentiary issues, trial briefs, and proposed findings for bench trials) plus exhibit binders. Also e-file the stipulated instructions and email Word versions to the case manager. Exchange marked exhibits 3 days before trial; on day one give the cour

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — TROs and preliminary injunctions
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. TROs and preliminary injunctions: The court strictly follows Rule 65 and LR 65.1 and rarely grants a TRO without notice. Phone the case manager on filing; a status conference usually follows quickly. Preliminary-injunction scheduling order: a substantive meet-and-confer, preferably in person, on narrower relief, agreed facts, and evidence; then a Joint Exhibit and Witness List (will/may call, short testimony summary, time estimates, objections), a marked Joint Exhibit Book, a Pre-Hearing Brief with numbered proposed findings and conclusions, and a joint statement on Rule 65(a)(2) consolidation. Evidence not on the list is excluded absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Removal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Removal (trap): After removal, each party must re-file on the docket, as separate entries, all state-court answers, amended and responsive pleadings, pending motions, and related briefs. Unresolved state-court motions not re-filed will not be considered, and LR 7.1(e) governs any remaining briefing. Remand motions for procedural defects must be filed within 30 days of the notice of removal; oral argument is typically held. Removal concerns are raised by order to show cause.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Protective orders and sealing: Stipulated protective orders must include the page’s required language stating that the order does not authorize sealed filings and listing the LR 5.3 contents of a sealing motion or stipulation. With any sealing request, submit through Utilities a proposed order stating the particular reason for the seal.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Settlement: The court routinely holds at least one settlement conference and expects settlement discussions throughout. A brief status conference on settlement is held shortly after discovery closes, and parties may stipulate to case evaluation or mediation at any time.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: Counsel meet and confer within 10 days of arraignment, or the government files the 03-AO-027 discovery notice. A signed Rule 11 plea agreement is due by the plea cutoff. Motions in limine and notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis are due at least 7 days before the final pretrial conference, with item-by-item reasons, or objections may be precluded. Exhibits use yellow government (numbers) and blue defense (letters) stickers; witnesses, including officers, testify in plain clothes. Submit agreed instructions (Sixth Circuit patterns where applicable) and disputed instructions with alternates or objections directly to chambers. Bench-trial findings are due 1 week before trial; the defendant must attend the final pretrial conference; exhibits, briefs, and instructions are filed within 5 business days of t

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Motions and hearings (trap): The clerk sends the hearing notice; no briefing schedule is issued. Motions are heard about two months after filing. L.R. 7.1 response and reply deadlines are enforced even when the hearing is far off (timely extension requests are routinely granted), and a party that fails to respond on time may not argue. Replies are accepted under L.R. 7.1; sur-replies are not permitted. Strict L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence is required, and the court may impose costs for noncompliance. Proposed orders at the hearing are encouraged. To exceed 25 pages, file an ex parte application with a copy of the proposed brief; extensions are rarely more than 5 extra pages for responses and 2 for replies.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment: Support each fact in the statement of material facts with citations to pleadings, discovery, depositions, affidavits, or documents, and file the full text of cited sources as an indexed appendix. Skip boilerplate standards and string cites; focus on a few recent, controlling cases. Copies of main cases with relevant passages highlighted and tabbed are encouraged, and copies of unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions must be submitted with the brief. Cite depositions by page and line; complete transcripts are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: Discovery generally runs 3 to 6 months from the answer. All witnesses, lay and expert, must be disclosed 1 month before the discovery cutoff. Discovery motions are generally referred to the magistrate judge (no blanket referral); after referral, communicate only with that chambers. The court will not order discovery after the cutoff. Discovery may be extended by stipulation, before or after the cutoff and without a motion, only if the motion cutoff, final pretrial conference, and trial dates are unaffected; other changes need a timely written motion. The court may take telephone calls on disputes arising during a deposition.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Conferences, removal, and TROs
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Conferences, removal, and TROs: A scheduling conference sets cutoffs and pretrial, trial, pretrial-order, and instruction dates. Status and pretrial conferences may be by telephone for out-of-town counsel, and otherwise with prior approval. The court does not remand sua sponte (L.R. 81.1); an order to show cause issues if removal looks improper, and oral argument is typically held on remand motions. For TROs and preliminary injunctions, the court consults counsel and sets a shortened schedule by written order.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Mediation and settlement
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Mediation and settlement: Diversity cases are not routinely sent to L.R. 16.3 mediation; referral occurs after the discovery cutoff only if the parties stipulate to mediation sanctions, by the scheduling-order date, and counsel must complete mediation before the final pretrial conference. The judge routinely participates in settlement in jury cases and refers non-jury cases to another judge. Settlement is discussed at the final pretrial conference, and a settlement conference can be requested at any stage.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial order and conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial order and conference (trap): Counsel confer face to face; plaintiff drafts the joint final pretrial order under L.R. 16.2. The scheduling order requires it at least 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with an original and one copy to chambers. Pending motions needing pretrial decision must be flagged by then. Witness-list additions are allowed only in exceptional circumstances. Parties must attend the final pretrial conference with trial counsel, who must have full authority to discuss settlement without further client approval, unless other arrangements are approved in advance. The conference is typically 1 to 2 weeks before trial. Foundation or authenticity objections not raised before trial are waived.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Trial submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Trial submissions (trap): Motions in limine: the page says at the final pretrial conference or 2 weeks before trial, whichever comes first; the scheduling order says 1 week before the trial term. Jury instructions: the page says the court gives counsel its standard opening and closing instructions at the final pretrial conference, and the joint instructions, joint verdict form, and separate disputed instructions (with each side’s support or objection) are due on the first day of trial, on paper and electronically. The scheduling order instead requires stipulated instructions 1 week before trial. At least 1 week before trial: voir dire requests and a statement of claims or defenses of no more than 2 pages. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions are filed before trial (the order says 1 week before), on paper and electronically.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Trailing docket; report trial conflicts as soon as discovered (the earliest notice has priority). Hours are set week by week. Openings and closings are limited to 30–60 minutes, and repetitive or cumulative evidence may be limited. Ask permission to approach a witness or the bench; bench conferences are discouraged. Exchange exhibits 1 week before trial; bench book required. The page says plaintiff numbers from 1 and defendant from 500 (the order says each party starts at 1); traditional stickers preferred. Parties keep custody of exhibits during trial and pending appeal. Resolve evidentiary and foundation issues before trial; do not bring record keepers when business-record authenticity is not really disputed. Trial will not be adjourned for last-minute depositions.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Jury selection: Strike method; the court conducts voir dire with limited follow-up by counsel, and counsel may not ask about the amount of damages sought. Three peremptories per party in civil cases, exercised in open court; a pass counts as an exercise. No alternates in civil trials; all seated jurors deliberate. The jury is charged before closing arguments and gets copies of the instructions. Juror questionnaires are allowed on motion for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: One or two alternates; defendant 10 peremptories, government 6. Pretrial conferences and arraignments on information are typically referred to a magistrate judge. Trial briefs are welcome but not required, and early Jencks disclosure is urged. Alford and nolo contendere pleas are rare and never accepted over government objection. Guideline disputes are typically resolved at a hearing before sentencing, and self-reporting is typically permitted.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Courtesy hard copies are always required. Under the case management order, deliver a copy of all motions and briefs to chambers by first-class mail or hand delivery the same day you e-file. Copies must be one-sided, with tabbed exhibits and an index of exhibits, and bound so the CM/ECF header shows on every page. No top fasteners, prong fasteners, side staples, loose pages, or single binder clips; a three-ring binder is preferred, though a short filing may be stapled in the top left corner or bound on the side. Staple the motion and brief separately from the exhibits, and start the brief on a separate page.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Briefs and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Briefs and format (trap): All filings, including exhibits, must be in 14-point font (L.R. 5.1(a)(3)). Every motion, response, and reply must include a table of contents, a table of authorities, and an index. Cite deposition testimony by page and line and attach the entire transcript, printed one page per page, with the relevant passages highlighted. File the full text of any unpublished source in an indexed appendix with the relevant portion highlighted or underlined. No string citations without at least parenthetical explanation; focus on a few recent, controlling cases. Ex parte applications to exceed 25 pages are rarely granted.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Motion practice
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Motion practice: Strict compliance with L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence; the court will strike papers and impose costs for noncompliance. L.R. 7.1(d) and (e) response deadlines are enforced, and the court sends notice of any hearing. If the parties resolve an issue in a pending motion, notify the court immediately by email to the case manager or fax to chambers. Proposed and stipulated orders go through CM/ECF Utilities/Proposed Orders and are not docketed. TROs and preliminary injunctions: the court sets the schedule and, absent extraordinary circumstances, requires some notice to the other side and a chance for both sides to be heard. Conferring first is strongly encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment and expert challenges (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment and expert challenges (trap): Absent extraordinary circumstances shown by motion, summary judgment motions may be filed only after fact and expert discovery close, and only one per party, addressing all counts within the page limits. Challenges to experts under Rules 702, 703, or 705 are due no later than the summary judgment deadline (typically 45 days after all discovery closes).

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Discovery and scheduling: Typical schedule: initial disclosures 45 days after the Rule 26(f) conference; amendments 30 days after the scheduling order; fact discovery 6–9 months; witness lists exchanged and proponent expert disclosures 60 days before the fact cutoff; rebuttal expert disclosures 30 days before; expert discovery closes 45 days after the fact cutoff. Start discovery once the case is joined; don’t wait for a scheduling order. Extending the cutoff takes a motion or stipulation to the district judge, and approval should not be presumed. L.R. 37.1 is strictly enforced. Discovery motions and deposition disputes usually go to the assigned magistrate judge; once referred, direct all communication to that judge’s chambers.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Motions in limine (trap): Due typically 60 days before the final pretrial conference. Each motion must cite and explain case law, not just a Rule of Evidence number. Before filing, the parties must meet and confer on each and every potential motion and try to stipulate. Each motion must state that the conference occurred and that the parties were absolutely unable to resolve the issue.

The parties themselves (natural persons and representatives of other parties) must attend the final pretrial conference with full settlement authority. docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — ERISA benefits cases
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. ERISA benefits cases: Review is on the administrative record under Wilkins, and Rule 56 procedures are not used. Each party files a “Statement of Procedural Challenge” or “Statement of No Procedural Challenge” 3 weeks after the order; a procedural challenge suspends later deadlines pending a conference on limited discovery. Defendant serves the administrative record (with the plan and summary plan description) in 3 weeks; standard-of-review statements are due in 1 month; cross-motions to reverse or affirm, with a joint appendix, are due in 4 months; responses 1 month later and replies 2 weeks after that. Deliver a single bound courtesy copy at e-filing (not with a top hole-punch binder).

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal and compassionate release
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Criminal and compassionate release: Pretrial matters are generally not referred to a magistrate judge. The court may accept Alford or nolo contendere pleas, always requires a presentence report, and enforces a firm plea cutoff. Criminal juries are generally 14; juror questionnaires may be allowed in high-profile or complex cases; peremptory allocation in multi-defendant trials is set at the final pretrial conference. No criminal trial brief is required, and the government is urged to disclose Jencks material before trial. Compassionate release exhibits must be numbered sequentially across the whole packet, indexed by exhibit, category, and page numbers, and highlighted on the relevant material.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Other: The court often refers civil cases to facilitation. Local counsel is required for attorneys who are not members of the State Bar of Michigan. Fed. R. Civ. P. 55(a) is strictly followed before a default judgment. If removal looks improper, the court issues an order to show cause or dismisses a facially invalid removal petition, and may hear argument.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Jurisdiction review (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Jurisdiction review (trap): The court reviews jurisdiction in every case. In a diversity case that does not plead each party’s citizenship or the amount in controversy, expect an order to show cause why the case should not be dismissed or remanded. Raise jurisdictional objections as soon as possible.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling conference
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling conference: A Notice of Scheduling Conference issues when the Answer is filed. If 3 weeks pass after the Answer without a notice, call the case manager. The conference is off the record in chambers in Port Huron, with trial counsel; responsible parties are occasionally required, and a phone conference is sometimes allowed. If trial counsel cannot attend, substitute counsel with complete working knowledge and decision authority must appear; a new date can sometimes be arranged with the case manager.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Rule 26(f) plan (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Rule 26(f) plan (trap): Plaintiff must organize the meet-and-confer and file a Rule 26(f)(3) plan at least 7 days before the conference. Corporate parties must file the LR 83.4 disclosure statement at least 7 days before it. Come prepared, after consulting clients, to narrow the issues, including withdrawing without prejudice claims and defenses not presently sustainable (the notice stresses that “failure to state a claim” is not a defense), and to state each claim’s and defense’s elements and good-faith factual basis. Also address entity parties, jurisdiction, related cases, amendments, experts, discovery, the Model ESI Order, ADR, consent, bench trial, dispositive motions, and settlement.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Suggested plan outline
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Suggested plan outline: The court’s sample outline asks for summaries of claims and defenses (not reprinted pleadings), any claims or defenses withdrawn without prejudice, a discovery plan, and the case’s complexity tier. It requires a discovery budget: each side’s estimated discovery costs, including attorney fees, with counsel stating the client was specifically advised and approved. Include an estimate of in-court hours for each side; the outline notes an ordinary personal-injury case should need about 20 hours. In a non-jury case, do not reveal strategy that could affect the court’s impartiality.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery timelines
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Discovery timelines: Simple case: discovery closes about 2 to 3 months after it starts, with resolution in under a year from the Answer. Standard case: 4 to 5 months, about one year. Complex case: 6 to 8 months, under two years. Highly complex case: at the court’s discretion, with counsel invited to propose a timeline. Counsel are encouraged to begin Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures and discovery by mutual consent before the conference.

docs.t: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland (E.D. Mich.) — Magistrate judge consent
docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Magistrate judge consent: The court will consider unanimous consent to full magistrate-judge jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) and Rule 73, using the standard consent form. The notice points out that magistrate judges have no felony trials, so an earlier and more certain trial date is likely.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Contacting chambers: The court strongly prefers email to the case manager, Tara Villereal (Tara_Villereal@mied.uscourts.gov), with opposing counsel copied. To adjourn a date, confer first and send a single email listing agreed dates that work for everyone. Ex parte contact with the case manager is allowed only on scheduling or administrative matters; contact with law clerks needs the court’s express approval. Counsel may ask the case manager for a telephone, Zoom, or Teams status conference to resolve disputes without motion practice.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Brief format and certification (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Brief format and certification (trap): Append the Brief Format Certification Form to the back of every brief, or the brief will be stricken. It certifies an L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence statement, 14-point font including footnotes, true double spacing (not “Exactly 28 pt”) and one-inch margins, no more than 10 footnotes, searchable PDFs, full (not minuscript) transcripts, and a courtesy copy if 50 pages or more. More than 10 footnotes means the brief is stricken; case and statute citations go inline. Every fact statement needs a pincite. The first party to cite a document attaches all of it, and others cite the docketed copy as (ECF No. ##, PageID.###-###). Do not attach unpublished cases available on Westlaw or Lexis, and do not file a motion inside a response brief without permission.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Mail a courtesy copy only if a brief and its exhibits total 50 or more pages: the e-filed version with CM/ECF headers, spiral or three-ring bound, printed single-sided, with exhibits tabbed.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Motions (trap): Excess pages are discouraged; seek them by motion for leave at least one day before the deadline for fewer than five pages and at least one week before for five or more, or the motion may be struck or denied. Responses and replies follow L.R. 7.1(e) unless the court says otherwise; a motion without a timely response is treated as unopposed. Motions to amend must attach a redlined proposed pleading (L.R. 15.1). Leave is required for more than one summary judgment motion (L.R. 7.1(b)).

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): The supporting brief must begin with a “Statement of Material Facts” in numbered paragraphs with record citations. The opposition must begin with a “Counter-statement of Material Facts” using matching numbers, admitting or contesting each fact with record citations, and may add a separately headed “Statement of Additional Material Facts.” If additional facts are raised, the reply must begin with a “Reply to Counter-statement of Material Facts” using the opponent’s numbering. All of these statements count toward the page limit.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion until: (1) a good-faith meet and confer (an email exchange is not enough; refusing to make yourself available may draw sanctions); (2) an email to the case manager requesting a telephone conference, with a concise summary and a certification that step 1 is done, and each side’s one-page summary exchanged and submitted through CM/ECF Utilities at least 24 hours before; (3) only then a motion, which the court decides or refers to the magistrate judge. The motion must attach the complete requests and responses and, for a completed deposition, the full (not minuscript) transcript. Noncompliance can draw costs and fees. docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling conference and plan
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling conference and plan: After an answer, the court orders a Rule 16 scheduling conference on the parties’ Rule 26(f) report and enters a scheduling order at or right after it; if a motion to dismiss is filed, the conference may wait until it is decided. The Joint Discovery Plan template covers counsel attending, jurisdiction, the case (including any forum-selection, choice-of-law, or arbitration clauses, quoted), voluntary exchanges, discovery and ESI, contemplated dispositive motions, ADR, and trial length (counted in days from 8:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.). docs.t: Judge Robert J. White (E.D. Mich.) — TROs, preliminary injunctions, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Robert J. White, E.D. Mich.. TROs, preliminary injunctions, and ADR: The court strictly follows Rule 65 and L.R. 65.1 and rarely grants a TRO without notice. Phone the case manager (the page gives 313-234-5180) when filing a TRO or preliminary injunction motion; a status conference follows to set a schedule. The example preliminary injunction order sets a response 5 days after the conference, a meet and confer on narrower relief, stipulations, and evidentiary objections, then a Joint Exhibit and Witness List, a marked Joint Exhibit Book, and a Pre-Hearing Brief with numbered proposed findings and conclusions and a joint Rule 65(a)(2) consolidation statement. Evidence not on the joint list is excluded absent good cause. Settlement status conferences are held at the case mid-point and near the close of discovery.
